newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end higher, seen hesitant.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end higher, seen hesitant.

text.p: Argentine stocks drifted in a narrow band and closed with moderate gains Tuesday, halting a two-session pullback, but traders remained cautious.

"The market recovered although it lost some of its momentum towards the close and we can expect more volatility tomorrow in view of the erratic performance of the U.S. markets," said Antonio Carluccio at traders Hector Bacque.

The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV gained 0.7 percent to close at 838.71. It had shed 2.1 percent in the previous two sessions, hurt by a selloff in the U.S. Treasuries market on the back of stronger-than-expected payrolls data.
"The bolsa will remain conditioned by movements on the U.S. markets and also by reactions to the political alliance formed by opposition parties," Carluccio said.

He noted so far this year the market had ignored politics, but this could change if the alliance between the Radical and Frepaso parties changed the outlook for October legislative polls which the ruling Peronists had been slated to win.
Floor volume recovered to 31.1 million pesos from a paltry 17.9 million Monday, but over-the-counter turnover continued to ease to 78.1 million pesos from 88.5 million Monday.
"It's good that activity is picking up again, but I don't expect to see recent strong volumes of 40 million pesos yet because the market is regrouping," another dealer said.
The all-share index added 0.6 percent, with winners beating losers 37 to 16 and 21 issues closing flat.

Top MerVal risers were Banco Frances, steelmaker Siderca and real estate developer Irsa, up 3.0 percent, 2.6 percent and 1.9 percent, respectively. Losers were led by holding firm Comercial del Plata, off 3.3 percent, textile firm Alpargatas, off 1.7 percent, and cement stock Corcemar, down 1.6 percent.
